name: iotaori_aa
label: iota Ori Aa (Hatysa: O9 III + B0.8 III/IV, 29.13 d, e 0.745)
sources: Wikipedia infobox (read 2026-10-08), citing the BRITE + spectroscopy analysis of the eclipsing orbit (Pablo et al. 2017, MNRAS 467, 2494): P 29.13376 d, e 0.7452 (+0.0010/-0.0014), i 62.86 (+0.17/-0.14) deg, omega 122.15 +/- 0.11 deg, a 132.32 (+1.01/-0.96) Rsun; masses 23.18 (+0.57/-0.53) and 13.44 +/- 0.30 Msun; radii 9.10 (+0.12/-0.10) and 4.94 (+0.16/-0.23) Rsun; T_eff 31 000 K and 18 319 (+531/-758) K; distance 412 (+14/-13) pc
van Leeuwen 2007 (Hipparcos): parallax 1.40 +/- 0.22 mas = 714 (+140/-100) pc -- inconsistent with the orbit's 412 pc by a factor 1.7; no Gaia parallax (V 2.77)
Tertiary Ab (7.77 Msun, B2 subgiant) at 155 mas by speckle interferometry; iota Ori B (V 7) at 11 arcsec
notes: a = 132.32 Rsun = 0.6153 AU; at 412 pc that is 1.494 mas with the stars 0.205 and 0.111 mas across, separations 0.18-1.9 mas around the eccentric orbit (fringe periods 70-900 m at 650 nm). The fringe spacing measures a in mas; against a in AU from the orbit that is a geometric distance which decides between 412 and 714 pc in a night.

Anchor V 2.85 = the Aa1 + Aa2 light (system V 2.77 less the tertiary): Ab at 155 mas is inside any field stop and is taken as 7 % third light (campaign option third_light_fraction 0.07, from a B2 IV against O9 III + B0.8 III); B at 11 arcsec is excluded.
The O9 III primary has a wind and the pair is a colliding-wind X-ray binary: the fringe should be measured in red continuum (650 nm) rather than in H-alpha.
node_pa_deg 0 is ASSUMED (unknown). Claret & Bloemen 2011 Spica law for both components; NewEra does not cover these temperatures.
Parameters are the infobox's; check against Pablo et al. 2017 before observing.
assumptions: distance_pc (412 pc from the orbit solution; Hipparcos says 714)
Wikipedia-quoted parameters not yet checked against Pablo et al. 2017
